findings.title: Task 15 and Task 17 disagree on how the auto-init timeout is applied
findings.description: Task 15 first says `init()` runs with `{ timeoutMs: GUIDE_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS }`. It then says to "pass the timeout as an `init()` option" so that `sync()` keeps no time limit. That makes the timeout opt-in, which contradicts the signature it gives (`init(operationPath)`). Task 17 then calls `SubmoduleStrategy.init(operationPath)` with no option. If someone reads Task 15 as "opt-in", `ensureCheckout()` would run the fetch with no time limit. That silently breaks D10 (the auto-init fetch must be bounded), and no test would catch it: Task 16 and Task 18 never check that the timeout is passed. Fix: give Task 15 one exact signature, for example `init(path, opts?: { timeoutMs?: number })`. Have Task 17 pass `GUIDE_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS` explicitly, and add a Task 18 case that checks the timeout is forwarded.

findings.title: Task 4 commits while the MCP package may not typecheck
findings.description: Tasks 1 and 3 narrow `GuideMethod` to `'submodule' | 'clone' | 'tarball'`. But `guideTools.ts` still declares the zod enum `'manual'` and passes it into `manager.install()` until Task 7. Task 4's commit only checks `pnpm --filter @context-forge/core test`. So the first commit, and the one after Task 6, can leave `@context-forge/mcp-server` failing typecheck. The slice's Implementation Notes ask for "the full suite after step 1". Fix: either change the Task 4 commit check to `pnpm -r typecheck && pnpm -r test`, or move the minimal CLI/MCP type fixes into Task 3 and keep Task 7 for alias behaviour only.

findings.title: The `'error'` checkout branch is never tested
findings.description: The slice's Data Flow lists `'error' → throw` as a branch, and the Technical criteria ask for tests of "`ensureCheckout()` for each branch of the state machine". Task 11 moves that throw into `detect()`. That is a reasonable choice because `GuideInfo.checkout` has no `'error'` value, but it means every caller of `detect()` now inherits the throw, including `cf guides info`, `guide_status` and `install`. Neither Task 12 nor Task 18 tests the `'error'` path, and no task checks what the wider throw does to the read-only status commands. Fix: add one case, such as a gitlink path that is not a repo or git missing, where `detect()`/`ensureCheckout()` rejects with a clear message. Also state in Task 11 that `cf guides info` showing an error in this case is intended.

findings.title: The CLI warning for `manual` in shared config is never checked
findings.description: The slice requires: "A project whose shared config has `guide.git_strategy: manual` installs as tarball with the same warning." Task 6 only checks that core *reports* the alias. Task 7 adds the stderr print in `guidesInstallAction()`, but Task 8 only tests the `--strategy manual` flag. Nothing checks that the warning actually appears on stderr when the value comes from config. Fix: add one case to Task 8, with `guide.git_strategy: manual` in config, that checks for a tarball install and the deprecation line on stderr.

findings.title: MCP call sites are listed by line number instead of found with the grep D3 requires
findings.description: D3 says to grep for `createContextPipeline`, `resolvePromptFilePath` and `GUIDE_RELATIVE_PATH` in **both** `packages/cli/src` and `packages/mcp-server/src`, and cover every hit. Task 20 does this for the CLI. Task 22 instead names two lines (~57 and ~98) and does not say whether both `prompt_list` and `prompt_get` go through ~98. Task 23 only tests `context_build`. Fix: add the same grep step to Task 22, list the covered MCP tools in the commit body, and add one `prompt_get` or `prompt_list` case to Task 23.

findings.title: Commit markers are inside checkbox items instead of on plain `**Commit**:` lines
findings.description: The commit points are written inside checkbox success-criteria items ("Commit: `refactor(core): …`"), here and at lines 127, 153, 204, 224, 246, 276, 312, 333, 342, 373, 389 and 412. They are in sensible places: after a tested pair, about once per feature. But markers must be plain `**Commit**:` lines, never checkboxes, so task-checker and the commit cadence can find them. Fix: move each one to its own plain `**Commit**:` line after the task.

findings.title: Several tiny tasks could be merged
findings.description: Task 10's success criterion ("typecheck passes once Task 11 populates the field") means it cannot be finished on its own, so merge it into Task 11. Pairs with effort 1+1, Tasks 13/14 and 28/29, could each become one task that includes its test, the way Task 24 already does. That would cut the file from 32 to about 29 tasks without losing coverage.

findings.title: The `manual` grep in Task 7 is loose and adds an exception the slice doesn't list
findings.description: `grep -rn "manual"` also matches words like "manually" in comments. Its expected result also allows the MCP zod enum entry and the deprecation text, which the slice's Technical criterion ("no `'manual'` literal outside the alias table and enum") does not list. The slice's own Component Structure requires the MCP enum to accept `manual`, so this gap is in the design. Narrow the grep to `"'manual'"` and say that the MCP enum and the warning text are accepted exceptions.

findings.title: Task 17 doesn't give a signature for `ensureCheckout()`
findings.description: Task 17 says `operationPath` resolution "matches `getGuideContext()` in `guides.ts`". That is CLI code, which core cannot import. Say whether `ensureCheckout()` takes `operationPath` as an argument or reads it from how `GuideManager` was built. Task 22 (MCP) also needs that answer.

findings.title: Every functional criterion is covered and nothing is out of scope
findings.description: Fresh-clone build and `--json` (Tasks 19–21), read-only `guides info` (Task 24), the out-of-sync warning (Tasks 17/18/21), the alias via flag (Tasks 7/8), `cf init --strategy` (Tasks 26/27), shared help (Tasks 25/27), the managed notice and README (Tasks 28–30), failing on a malformed config (Tasks 5/6), and CHANGELOG/DEVLOG (Task 31) are all covered. Task 32 runs the verification walkthrough. Every task traces back to a design decision or a success criterion. No NFR is restated, so no load-test or CI-wiring task is needed.
